rationale: Evidence from the iteration 0 race (development simulator, 60 trials): every run ended off track, with progress of only 0.10 to 0.15, one line-loss event each, and max_error of about 0.062 m. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 m, so the robot reached the edge early and never got far. rms_error (0.025 to 0.029 m) is well below the limit, and steering_oscillation is low (0.08 to 0.14). The robot is therefore not weaving. It drifts steadily toward one edge and then drops off. A steady drift of this kind is the signature of the fixed left/right motor mismatch in the disturbance, which a proportional-only loop cannot fully remove. With ki = 0.05 the integral term is too weak to cancel it, and with kp = 2.0 the steady offset is still a few centimetres. I make two changes. First, I raise ki from 0.05 to 0.3, so the integral can cancel the constant bias. The integral is clamped at +/-2, so windup on the slalom stays bounded. Second, I raise kp from 2.0 to 2.5 to tighten tracking and keep max_error further from the 0.06 m limit. kd stays at 0.1 and I deliberately keep base_speed at 1.6, the sensor layout, and line_loss unchanged, so the cause of any change in the result is clear. Expected result: max_error falls below about 0.05 m, progress rises well past 0.15 on the oval and s-bend, and line_loss_events drops to 0 on the oval. If the robot still goes off track on the slalom, the next step is to widen the sensor span to x = +/-0.04 or to reduce base_speed. Hypotheses to check: (H1) the drift is a steady bias from the motor mismatch, so ki resolves it; (H2) the remaining failures are bend-entry overshoots, which kp and kd address. Measurements to watch: progress, max_error, line_loss_events, and steering_oscillation, which should stay low as kp rises.
